cards.label: The City — the Guild registry
cards.text: The door on the third floor does say STATIONERY. Behind it: a counter, a brass bell, a coat stand with no coats, and a woman writing in a ledger with a fountain pen.

cards.speaker: Wren
cards.text: She finishes the line before she looks up. "You'll be James's letter. He used the word 'adequate'. From James, that's practically a reference."

cards.speaker: Wren
cards.text: "We've already exchanged messages, of course. It's nice to put a face to the file."

cards.speaker: Wren
cards.text: She turns the ledger round to face you. "I'm registering you as an associate. Not a member. Members need a sponsor, a vote and a dinner nobody enjoys. Associates need a signature."

cards.speaker: Wren
cards.text: "Recipes. James sells his time and life work. Everything else, the Guild holds, and I keep the catalogue. The basic procedures are for sale to any associate. The finer notes depend on your standing."

cards.speaker: Ingram
cards.text: A door opens behind the counter. A tall man in a grey suit reads the ledger upside down without slowing. "Associate. Do keep that word in pencil, Registrar."
Wren waits for the door to close. Then she uncaps the pen again and writes your name in ink.

cards.speaker: Wren
cards.text: "Dr Ingram runs Assay. Standing is the slow part, because the Guild trusts what it has tested. So I'll send you commissions: a recipe, a grade, a date. Deliver well and the finer notes open up. Deliver late and Assay hears about it."

cards.speaker: Wren
cards.text: She blots the page. "I've spent eleven years getting an associate register past the Court. You're the fourth name in it. Please don't be the reason it closes."
She files the page under A, behind three others. The first commission will come by message. On your way out you pass a door marked ASSAY. It's shut, and the light is on.
